subject: A whole living anamu plant about a metre tall, thin stem going woody at the base, alternate oval pointed leaves, one flower spike leaning out of frame. Standing upright in shaded leaf litter and bare turned earth, with the ground falling away dark behind it.

A single fresh anamu leaf laid flat and slightly curled at one edge, filling most of the frame, close enough to read the midrib and the fine side veins. Nothing else in shot but the ground it rests on.

One washed anamu taproot, pale and tapering, woody and slightly fibrous at the crown, with a few cut side rootlets still attached. Laid on a diagonal with a short offcut beside it showing the pale cross section.

A single anamu flower spike, a long thin stalk carrying small greenish white flowers spaced along its length, arching from the lower left corner. A second spike behind it, out of focus, carrying the barbed green fruit.

A garlic bulb halved through the cloves, a red onion cut in half showing its rings, and a crushed green leaf bruised at the edges, arranged in a loose line with a little space between them. Papery garlic skin left where it fell.

Two small heaps of milled dried herb side by side, one greener and coarser, one paler and greyer and finer, each with a scattering of loose powder around its base. Shot slightly from above so both heaps read as texture.

The shaded margin of a tropical forest in the wet season: a worn earth track running along the edge, low broadleaved herbs crowding the disturbed ground beside it, tall trunks closing over the back of the frame.
